Regenerate the per-segment agent kit from the canonical source at the repository root, and
confirm the drift check passes.

The canonical kit lives in `.commandcode/` at the repository root (agents, skills, commands,
`AGENTS.md`) with per-segment memory authored under `tools/segments/`. The manifest at
`tools/agent-kit.manifest.json` maps what each segment receives. Generated files land in
`Backend/.commandcode/`, `Frontend/.commandcode/` and `Mobile app/.commandcode/`, each
carrying a `<!-- generated by tools/agent-kit.mjs ... -->` marker.

```bash
node tools/agent-kit.mjs
node tools/agent-kit.mjs --check
```

If this was a change to the kit itself (${ARGUMENTS:-no arguments given}):

- Confirm you edited the **canonical** file under `.commandcode/` or `tools/segments/`, never
  a generated copy.
- If you added an agent or skill, ensure its frontmatter is valid: agents use only the
  documented fields (`name`, `description`, `tools`, `disallowedTools`, `model`,
  `reasoningEffort`, `maxTurns`, `permissionMode`, `background`, `showOutput`); a skill's
  `name` must exactly match its directory name, and frontmatter must stay at the top of the
  file (the generator inserts its marker *after* the closing `---` for that reason).
- Add it to the relevant segment lists in `tools/agent-kit.manifest.json`.

Report which files were created, updated or removed, and the output of `--check`. If the
check fails, show the drift list verbatim.

Note: `.commandcode/taste/` is managed by the taste tool — never hand-edit it. The obsolete
`.agent/` directory is not a location Command Code reads (it reads `.agents/skills/`), so
kit content belongs under `.commandcode/`.
